newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria cuts price of cement by about 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria cuts price of cement by about 10 pct.

text.p: Nigeria's Finance Ministry said on Monday retail prices of cement in the country had come down because of reduced production costs through government reliefs.

"Among these are reduction in companies income tax from 35 to 30 percent, reduction in capital gains tax, across the board reduction in import duties by 35 percent and tax incentives for research and development," it said in a statement.

It said following a meeting with cement manufacturers on December 23rd they agreed to reduce their prices by 600 naira a tonne which translates to a cost of between 285 naira to 327 naira for a 50 kg bag depending on where in the country.
This works out at a reduction of about 10 percent.
There are nearly a dozen cement factories around Nigeria. Last year they were banned from importing gypsum and compelled to mine the raw material locally where it is abundant.
"Production of gypsum is now approaching the stage of glut in the market and this material is procured cheaply by cement manufacturing companies," the finance ministry statement said.
It said cement manufacturers from the beginning of this month had been selling the product at the new reduced costs and also directly to consumers rather than through middle men.
"The reduction of price will actually have a significant impact and reduce inflation in the country," it said.
